stack.single: one branch off trunk, 1 AI commit
stack.stack2_bot: 2-branch stack, change under test on the BOTTOM branch
stack.stack2_top: 2-branch stack, change under test on the TOP branch
stack.stack3_mid: 3-branch stack, change under test on the MIDDLE branch
stack.stack3_all: 3-branch stack, AI commits on ALL branches

attribution.committed: AI work committed with notes before the workflow
attribution.uncommitted: AI checkpoint in the working log, not yet committed
attribution.mixed: committed AI commit plus uncommitted AI edits on top
attribution.multifile: one commit touching 3 AI files (rename-adjacent shapes)

trunk.diverged: trunk advanced with non-overlapping changes (real restack)
trunk.overlap: trunk advanced touching the same file regions (conflict fuel)

observation.blind: rewrite phase executed raw (trace2 off), daemon restarted after -- reconciliation/replay territory

repeat.twice: run the workflow twice back-to-back (idempotency; second run is usually a no-op and must not disturb notes)

families.SYNC_FF: gt sync trunk fast-forward: fetch; update-ref trunk (or `reset -q --keep` when trunk/branch is checked out); stash create/ls-files snapshot around it
families.SYNC_RESTACK: gt sync with restack: fetch + trunk move, then per-branch synthetic-base commit-tree -> merge-tree --allow-unrelated-histories -> commit-tree(real msg) -> update-ref, bottom-up through the stack
families.RESTACK: gt restack without fetch: same rewrite core as SYNC_RESTACK, no remote
families.CREATE: gt create: stash-wrapped branch creation + commit (stash create; checkout -b; commit; metadata refs)
families.MODIFY: gt modify: amend HEAD (commit --amend shape) then restack descendants via the rewrite core
families.SUBMIT: gt submit: restack if needed, then push --force-with-lease... --no-verify --atomic per branch
families.CONFLICT_CONTINUE: restack hits a real conflict (merge-tree unresolvable / cleanRebaseMergeTree failure) -> gt falls back to real git rebase -> user resolves -> gt continue
families.CONFLICT_ABORT: same conflict entry, then gt abort -> git rebase --abort + gt state restore; branch must return to pre-workflow tip with notes intact
families.UNDO: gt undo of a completed restack: reset -q --keep <pre-restack-tip> moving the branch backward (fork-point-spanning ranges)
families.MOVE_ONTO: gt move --onto: rewrite core applied with a different parent (not trunk); descendants restacked
families.HOUSEKEEPING: gt checkout/track/trunk/info: metadata-only flows -- control group, must never touch attribution
families.FLAVOR_17X: gt 1.7.x shapes: hash-object -w --stdin storms + eager metadata update-refs interleaved into the SYNC_RESTACK core
families.WORKTREE: SYNC_RESTACK and MODIFY cores executed from a LINKED WORKTREE (.claude/worktrees pattern observed in production logs): per-worktree HEAD reflog, per-worktree working log, shared refs
families.REFSTDIN: SYNC_RESTACK core but all branch moves applied via a single `update-ref --stdin` batch (binary-evidenced flavor): the daemon sees ONE command move many refs
families.RENAME: AI commit renames a file (and edits it) then goes through the restack core; rename-following in note translation under merge-tree rewrites
families.MERGE_IN_STACK: a merge commit inside the stack (pull-merge shape) goes through the restack core; exercises derive_merge_commit_mappings
families.PARTIAL_STAGE: workflow starts with a working tree mixing staged AI edits, unstaged AI edits, and untracked files (`stash create` + ls-files snapshot boundary conditions)
families.LIFECYCLE: full-chain composites: create -> modify -> sync(restack) -> submit; create -> sync(conflict->continue) -> modify -> submit; create -> sync -> undo -> sync again; attribution must survive the entire chain end-to-end
families.NESTED_CONFLICT: conflicts at TWO stack levels in one sync: resolve+continue the first, then hit and resolve/abort the second
